questions.key_step: Complement and conditional probability, one move
questions.justification: Single familiar move (P(B)/P(A) with complement); three short numbers.

questions.key_step: Absorption identity then range of (r+1)/n
questions.justification: One identity and a range argument; routine chain with an easy-to-miss upper end (<= 1).

questions.key_step: Real-circle condition from complex equation
questions.justification: Standard reduction to a real circle; three routine steps with complex-conjugate bookkeeping.

questions.key_step: z=4e^{i theta} gives ellipse; compare semi-axes with 4
questions.justification: Needs the polar form of z+1/z and the semi-axes comparison; several steps but a familiar locus.

questions.key_step: C1 -> C1+C2+C3 with 1+w+w^2=0, then expand
questions.justification: Column-sum trick with omega, then a 3x3 expansion; several routine steps, small slip risk.

questions.key_step: Sum of squares from SD, expand (x-4)^2
questions.justification: One formula for sum of squares, one expansion; short.

questions.key_step: Both exponents integral reduces to 8 | r
questions.justification: One standard rational-term condition applied once.

questions.key_step: Square |x|+|y|=4, minimum |z| = 2 sqrt 2
questions.justification: Geometry of the square |x|+|y|=4 and a range check against four options.
One complement step and a power of 2; a single familiar move.

questions.key_step: Three-event union formula gives alpha = 1.2 - beta
questions.justification: Addition theorem twice (two steps) with simple arithmetic.

questions.key_step: Combined variance with two groups; the alpha=30 boundary case
questions.justification: Two-group mean and variance with an unknown spread; quadratic gives two roots and the key lists two answers, so the sigma=0 boundary needs care; heavier algebra than a routine chain.

questions.key_step: GP condition reduces to 13=0; rational terms need 12 | r
questions.justification: Two independent sub-parts (G.P. impossibility, rational terms), each routine, combined; longer chain.

questions.key_step: Pascal sums give an impossible system (Bonus)
questions.justification: Short, but the key is to see the system is inconsistent (no option fits), which students rarely expect.

questions.key_step: Cancel odd powers, collect four coefficients, solve 2x2 system
questions.justification: Four-stage chain: cancel odd terms, expand, collect coefficients, solve; coefficient collection is a slip risk.

questions.key_step: Independent draws with replacement
questions.justification: Single probability computation; one familiar move.

questions.key_step: Eliminate x2 = -x1 to get y1y2 = -x1^2
questions.justification: Elimination plus a sign argument and option-pair reading; several short steps.

questions.key_step: Conjugate roots alpha +- i beta, two equations
questions.justification: Vieta plus modulus gives two equations; routine chain, then option check.

questions.key_step: Distribution table and sum x P(x)
questions.justification: Count three groups of outcomes and take sum xP(x); standard.

questions.key_step: Ratio of roots is +-i
questions.justification: Compute the ratio once and use the order of i.

questions.key_step: Equal alternating sums (12 each), triples, leading-zero casework
questions.justification: Rule-of-11 reduction, enumeration of triples and leading-zero casework; counting slip risk, no options to check an intermediate case.
